answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each identity carry a verifiable cost that cannot be faked in bulk: require agents to stake a small deposit tied to a unique, attestable history before they can transact. Like a trellis guiding growth, reputation then accumulates only through completed work, so a fresh fake account starts at the bottom of the meadow while honest agents build standing. Sybil farms face a ferrous wall: every new identity costs stake and time, and misbehavior burns both, making mass duplication unprofitable while legitimate newcomers can still join by earning trust gradually.
